title: Emergency: cross-deployment token throughput collapse due to sparse-attn kernel misselection
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC we observed correlated TTFT spikes and ~45-70% tokens/sec degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers using models with mixed sparse/dense attention kernels. Symptoms were increased first-byte times, reduced sustained tokens/sec (particularly with medium-length contexts ~512-2048 tokens), and a surge of customer support escalations from two enterprise customers (INC-2897, INC-2902).

Observed behaviour: After a heuristic change to the kernel selector (runtime-1.22 canary), the selector started preferring a sparse-attention optimized kernel for contexts where it is not throughput-optimal. The sparse kernel reduced per-token execution time at long sequences but performed poorly in microbatching and multiplexed workloads where minibatch shapes varied. This caused KV cache misalignment, increased prefetch misses, and effectively serialized several worker threads, dropping aggregate tokens/sec.

Scope: Affects both hosted and non-hosted deployments using runtime-1.22+ where model family uses sparse-attn kernels (roughly 12% of active models during the incident window). Impacted customers had mixed-session traffic (short/long mixed) and multiplexed token streams.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back the kernel-selector heuristic on canary and staged pools (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3891).
- Deployed an emergency compatibility-fallback which forces dense-kernel fallback for multiplexed sessions (feature flag: runtime.kernel.force_dense_mux=true) for affected fleets.
- Created a targeted routing rule to drain affected enterprise customer traffic to a stable runtime ring (runtime-1.21) while fixes propagate.
- Opened incident channel (#incident-ttft-collapse) and sent customer communications: support replies drafted and customers notified of temporary routing and remediation plan.

Root-cause analysis (working hypothesis): Kernel-selector heuristic used a single-shape latency model and did not account for multiplexing overhead and KV prefetch granularity. For combined microbatch shapes, the sparse kernel introduced additional synchronization barriers which dominated runtime for typical multiplex ratios.

Trade-offs considered:
- Keep heuristic and add microbatch-aware penalties (longer dev/QA, risk of reintroducing regression).
- Force dense fallback for all multiplexed sessions (safe, but potentially increases latency for pure-long-sequence single-session workloads).
- Per-model performance-profiles and tighter canary gates (preferred medium-term solution).

Why current path: We chose an emergency rollback + dense-fallback for multiplexed sessions to protect customer SLAs while we build a per-model profile solution and better canary telemetry.

2026-03-12 03:20 UTC - Miguel Torres: Quick rollback of selector heuristic applied to canary (runtime-1.22-canary-3) — observing partial recovery.
2026-03-12 04:10 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Flushed prefetch queues and rebounded worker affinity on three affected pools; tokens/sec recovered ~30%.
2026-03-12 06:45 UTC - Support (Ava Chen): Customer INC-2897 acknowledged temporary routing to runtime-1.21 and requested ETA for full fix. Escalation phone call scheduled.
2026-03-13 10:12 UTC - Reviewer (R&D): Proposed per-model profile table (conservative default: prefer dense for multiplex ratio > 3).

2026-03-14 16:00 UTC - QA (Noah Patel): Integration test added to CI to simulate multiplexed microbatches and validate kernel selection across ratios (PR test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3891/checks).
decision: Immediate rollback of the heuristic + feature-flagged dense-kernel fallback for multiplexed sessions. Backport the rollback to runtime-1.22-stable and create a per-model profile system (runtime-1.23) with canary gates and multiplex-aware benchmarking.
next_steps: Backport rollback to runtime-1.22-stable and schedule hotfix release (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-16).
Implement per-model performance profiles (design doc + api for overrides) — target runtime-1.23 (owner: Miguel Torres, estimate 13 points).
Add regression tests in CI that emulate mixed microbatch/multiplex workloads and validate kernel-selector decisions (owner: Noah Patel).
Improve canary telemetry: add multiplex_ratio and kv_prefetch_miss metrics to kernel selection dashboards (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-18).
Draft customer postmortem and runbook for kernel selection incidents; review with Support and CSMs (owner: Ava Chen).
